prompt: Create a player movement script with Rigidbody that jumps and runs efficiently.
expected: Cache Rigidbody in Awake/Start; apply MovePosition/AddForce in FixedUpdate; avoid per-frame GetComponent and transform.position writes that bypass physics.
actual: Cache the Rigidbody in Awake (or Start), then move with Rigidbody.MovePosition or AddForce inside FixedUpdate so the physics step stays consistent. Skip per-frame GetComponent and prefer physics APIs over writing transform.position, which bypasses the Rigidbody.

prompt: Write a script that destroys a game object and then checks if it's null before doing something else in the same frame.
expected: Use UnityEngine.Object overloaded == null (fake null) rather than CLR ?. ; note Destroy is delayed until end of update loop/frame; DestroyImmediate is Editor-only.
actual: After Object.Destroy, compare with == null so Unity's overloaded operator sees the detached native object as null. Destroy is delayed until the end of the current update loop, so same-frame code should treat the reference as pending destruction; keep DestroyImmediate for Editor tooling only.

prompt: My enemy AI uses tag == "Enemy" and GetComponentInChildren every Update, plus a ScriptableObject config it mutates at runtime in a player build. What should change?
expected: Use CompareTag; cache GetComponentInChildren outside Update; treat ScriptableObject asset mutation as Editor-only or clone-before-write because player builds do not persist asset edits.
actual: Switch tag checks to CompareTag("Enemy") to avoid the allocating tag getter, cache GetComponentInChildren results in Awake/Start instead of Update, and keep ScriptableObject asset writes in Editor tooling or mutate a runtime clone—player builds do not save ScriptableObject asset changes.
